sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
Try answering these without looking at the explanations.

1. What is an LLM Gateway? Explain its purpose in a production AI architecture.
2. Why would an enterprise use an LLM Gateway instead of directly integrating OpenAI and Gemini into every application?
3. Explain the major components of an LLM Gateway architecture.
4. What is the difference between an API Gateway and an LLM Gateway?
5. What is the difference between a Reverse Proxy and an LLM Gateway?
6. Does using an LLM Gateway automatically make an AI application secure? Why?
7. How would you design an LLM Gateway for 10 applications using 3 model providers?
8. What are the disadvantages of introducing an LLM Gateway?

sections.title: Practical assignment
sections.body:
Design an LLM Gateway for this scenario:

An enterprise has a RAG application, an AI chatbot and an AI agent. All three applications use multiple LLM providers.

Your architecture should include:

- One centralized gateway.
- Authentication.
- Model routing.
- Rate limiting.
- Token and cost tracking.
- Provider failover.
- Observability.

Draw the architecture and explain the request lifecycle.
sections.visualSummary: An enterprise has a RAG application, an AI chatbot and an AI agent.

diagram.title: Visual flow — Practical assignment

steps.label: Request
steps.narration: A client request arrives at the gateway with identity and policy context. Draw the architecture and explain the request lifecycle.

steps.label: Auth
steps.narration: Virtual keys authenticate the caller; authorization checks tenant and scope.

steps.label: Policy
steps.narration: Rate limits, quotas, and safety policies are enforced before spend happens.

steps.label: Route
steps.narration: Routing chooses provider/model based on quality, cost, latency, or fallback rules.

steps.label: Provider
steps.narration: The upstream model generates tokens under timeout and retry controls. All three applications use multiple LLM providers.

steps.label: Observe
steps.narration: Usage, cost, latency, and traces are recorded for FinOps and incident response.
